admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the act of Congress approved on 28 February 1806 'To suspend the commercial intercourse between the United States, and certain parts of the island of St. Domingo': trade with any part of the island 'not in possession, and under the acknowledged government of France, shall be, and is hereby prohibited'. A law.
label: The act of 28 February 1806 suspending trade with parts of St. Domingo

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of John Quincy Adams's letter of 8 June 1808 to the Massachusetts legislature, resigning his seat in the Senate after the legislature had passed resolutions disapproving of measures he had supported.
label: John Quincy Adams resigns from the Senate

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of the address or the answer, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of Vice President Adams's farewell address to the Senate (15 February 1797), plus the Senate's answer where printed separately.
label: Adams's farewell to the Senate

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of the speech text, checked against the scan (opening only).
definition: Printings of President Adams's speech of 16 May 1797 opening the special session of Congress. Pages that only quote phrases from it are not included.
label: Adams's speech to Congress

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of this report, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Civitavecchia report (30 June 1797) of a battle near Messina between an Algerine cruiser and a ship of the King of the Two Sicilies. The battle itself is not independently verified.
label: Algerine–Sicilian sea battle

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: A New Bedford report of February 1808 that Algiers had declared war on the United States, the American consul general's circular of the same weeks that the dispute was settled, and a June report of the Dey's new demands. Contains those three groups.
label: Algiers and the American ships, 1808

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two items from Algiers printed from September to November 1805: a Salem report, by way of Leghorn, of an insurrection at Algiers, and the letter of 9 September of the American charge d'affaires at Algiers that 'the soldiers rose in a body and murdered the Dey'. Contains those two groups.
label: Reports from Algiers, 1805

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a New Bedford handbill of 30 January 1808: the ship Honestus, 42 days from the Downs, had been told off Cape Trafalgar that Algiers had declared war against America and captured American vessels. It is a report; the consul general's circular, printed in the same weeks, says the dispute had been settled.
label: New Bedford: 'War with Algiers'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter from Alicante of 27 March 1808, received at Boston and introduced as 'interesting particulars of the affairs of Spain': a rumour that the royal family meant to leave for Cadiz and embark on the English squadron brought crowds to the palace at Aranjuez; the Prince of Peace fell, and the King resigned his crown to his son. One paper prints only its later part.
label: Alicante letter: 'a rumour being spread at Aranjuez'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of another letter from Alicante of 27 March 1808, which reached Boston by the brig Sally: on the evening of 18 March the Prince of Peace ordered the Spanish and Walloon guards to Aranjuez; a report that the royal family meant to flee to Gibraltar and America brought a crowd to the palace crying 'kill the traitor'.
label: Alicante letter: the guards ordered to Aranjuez

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two letters from Alicante, both dated 27 March 1808, on the rising at Aranjuez and the fall of the Prince of Peace, as American papers printed them in May 1808, several of them side by side ('Extract of another Letter'). Contains those two groups. Each is one letter-writer's account.
label: Revolution in Spain: two letters from Alicante

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from Daniel Crommelin and Sons, Amsterdam, 30 December 1807, received at New York on 13 February 1808: official news of a decree of the French Emperor at Milan under which vessels that had submitted to British search or paid duties in Britain were to be treated as denationalised. It is a merchant house's summary, not the decree.
label: An Amsterdam letter on the Milan decree

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of President Jefferson's annual message to Congress of 2 December 1806: 'It would have given me, fellow citizens, great satisfaction to announce, in the moment of your meeting, that the difficulties in our foreign relations, existing at the time of your last separation, had been amicably and justly terminated'. The executive's own account of the year.
label: The President's annual message of 2 December 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from the master of an American vessel, dated Antigua, 28 December 1805, first printed in the Norfolk Gazette, which had it from 'a mercantile friend': 'Every American vessel coming from a French Island, with cargo, is certain to be carried in'. One writer's account; it alleges that 'a junto consisting of the Judge, the Lawyers, the owners of privateers' shares the costs charged to Americans.
label: A shipmaster's letter from Antigua: American vessels carried in

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from a house in Antwerp to one in Bordeaux (28 September 1807), brought by the Sally-Barker-Windsor: 'We understand' that the Emperor had ordered every vessel bound to or from England to be captured, 'a mortal blow to the American commerce'. It reports a rumoured order.
label: An Antwerp letter: ships to or from England to be taken

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Boston Gazette report of 5 September 1808: the ship Arcturus, 48 days from St. Sebastian, had arrived with P. R. Livingston, bearer of dispatches from the French government, and with passengers' accounts that General Dupont had been defeated at Cordova and Andujar. A report from passengers ('is said').
label: News from Spain by the Arcturus

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the armistice between the French and Russian armies agreed at Tilsit on 21 June 1807 (signed by Berthier and Prince Labanoff), the preliminary to the peace.
label: Armistice between France and Russia

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a copy of a letter of General Armstrong, the American minister at Paris, 23 February 1809: 'His Majesty has been pleased to raise the Embargo on American vessels within the ports of France and her dependencies and (the better to assure their direct return to the United States) to place them altogether at my disposition.' The American minister's report.
label: General Armstrong's letter of 23 February 1809: the French embargo raised

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of General Armstrong's letter to the Secretary of State from Bourbon l'Archambault, 28 August 1808, sent to Congress with the President's message: he would not return to Paris to renew his discussions with Champagny, being convinced that a new attempt would be useless and probably injurious.
label: Armstrong to Madison, 28 August

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The papers of April 1809 on the arrangement between the Secretary of State, Robert Smith, and the British minister, David Montague Erskine, as the papers printed them: the National Intelligencer's paragraph of 19 April, the notes exchanged on 17, 18 and 19 April, the President's proclamation of 19 April renewing trade with Great Britain from 10 June, and the Secretary of State's answer to the Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce. Contains those four groups. Official documents and the government paper's account.
label: The arrangement with the British minister, April 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The two armies' own accounts of the battle fought on 21 and 22 May 1809 near Vienna, on the left bank of the Danube, as American papers printed them in July and August from London papers: a London summary of the French tenth bulletin, and the Austrian official bulletin published by order of the Archduke Charles. Contains those two groups. Each is one side's account.
label: The battle on the Danube, 21 and 22 May 1809: the French and the Austrian bulletins

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Four accounts of the battle of 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz, between the French army and the armies of Russia and Austria, as American papers printed them in February and March 1806: a notice of the British government, a letter of Marshal Berthier, the French army's thirtieth bulletin, and the Emperor's proclamation to his army. Each is one side's account. Contains those four groups.
label: The battle of Austerlitz in the papers, 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two Austrian state papers of April 1809 that American papers printed in June from London papers: the Emperor Francis's declaration on leaving Vienna, and the Archduke Charles's address to the German nation. Contains those two groups. Each is the Austrian government's own statement.
label: Austria goes to war, April 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an address to the German nation that, as the papers print it, 'The Archduke Charles has issued': 'His Majesty the Emperor of Austria is forced to take up arms, because the French Emperor will not tolerate the existence of a State which does not acknowledge his supremacy of power'. The Austrian side's own statement.
label: The Archduke Charles's address to the German nation, April 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the Austrian army's bulletin 'Published by order of his Imperial Highness, the Archduke Charles': 'the following preliminary report of the brilliant victory obtained the 21st and 22nd of May, is issued on the 23rd from the head quarters at Breitenlee'. Most papers head it 'AUSTRIAN OFFICIAL BULLETIN OF THE DEFEAT OF THE FRENCH'. The Austrian army's own account.
label: The Austrian official bulletin of the battle, 23 May 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the President's message delivered to both Houses on 20 March 1804 by Mr. Harvie: 'I communicate to Congress a letter received from captain Bainbridge, commander of the Philadelphia frigate, informing us of the wreck of that vessel on the coast of Tripoli, and that himself, his officers and men, have fallen into the hands of the Tripolitans'; it asks for an addition to the naval appropriation. Most papers print with it the captain's letter, dated Tripoli, 1 November 1803: 'Misfortune necessitates me to make a communication the most distressing of my life'. The Kentucky Gazette printed the letter in its next issue. The President's message, and the captain's own account.
label: The President's message of 20 March 1804 with Captain Bainbridge's letter on the loss of the frigate Philadelphia

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of Commodore Barney's letter of 21 August 1797 on escaping a seven-month blockade.
label: Barney escapes the blockade

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of 'an extract of a letter from Commodore Barron to William Eaton, Esq. dated Malta, March 22, 1805', released at Washington in September: 'You must be sensible that in giving their sanction to a co-operation with the Ex-Bashaw, government did not contemplate the measure as leading necessarily and absolutely to a re-instatement of that Prince'; he withholds his sanction from any convention binding the United States to place the Ex-Bashaw on the throne. The commodore's own instructions and reasoning.
label: Commodore Barron's letter to William Eaton, 22 March

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of Captain John Barry's letter to John Hancock or the Marine Committee ('In sight of the Capes of Virginia, April 7, 1776'): he fell in with the sloop Edward, belonging to the Liverpool frigate, and took her after a fight of near two glasses.
label: Barry takes the Edward

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of General Bennigsen's report to the King of Prussia on the battle of Pultusk (26 December 1806), the Russian official account, in which he writes that he repulsed the French attack on every point.
label: Bennigsen's account of Pultusk

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the order of Vice-Admiral George Cranfield Berkeley, British commander in chief at Halifax (1 June 1807), directing the captains under his command, if they met the Chesapeake at sea, to show her captain the order and search her for the deserters named in its margin. American papers printed it from late July.
label: Admiral Berkeley's order

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter from General Berthier, chief of the staff of the army of Italy, to General Baraguey d'Hilliers (each paper spells the name differently), dated at Milan, 8 Frimaire, 28 November 1796: 'I informed you, general, by the last bulletin which I sent you, that, after having beaten the troops commanded by general Alvinzy in person, at Arcola, the commander in chief made his dispositions to attack the column commanded by general Davidovich'; it reports that the enemy was driven from the heights of Rivoli with 1,100 prisoners taken. A staff officer's own report for the French side.
label: General Berthier's letter from Milan, 28 November 1796: the army of Italy after Arcola

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter of Marshal Berthier, the French minister of war and major general of the Grand Army, to Marshal Massena, on the battle of 2 December 1805, translated for the Baltimore American from papers brought from Leghorn: 'I am impatient, marshal, to send you' the news of the battle. The French army's own account.
label: Marshal Berthier's letter to Marshal Massena on the battle

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter from Bishop Moore, dated Thursday evening, 12 July 1804, to Mr. Coleman of the New York Evening Post: 'The public mind being extremely agitated by the melancholy fate of that great man, Alexander Hamilton, I have thought it would be grateful to my fellow citizens, would provide against misrepresentation, and, perhaps, be conducive to the advancement of the cause of religion, were I to give a narrative of some facts which have fallen under my own observation, during the time which elapsed between the fatal duel and his departure out of this world.' The bishop's own account of his visits and of the communion he gave.
label: Bishop Moore's letter to the Evening Post, 12 July 1804, on General Hamilton's last hours

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The Blount affair in the 1797 papers: the letter made public (July), Blount's welcome home at Knoxville (September), and the House committee's report (December). Contains those three groups; the wider coverage is not included.
label: Blount affair

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Reports of the House committee's evidence report on Blount, 4 December 1797: a fuller account and a shorter summary.
label: House committee report on Blount

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Knoxville report (18 September 1797) of Blount's welcome home.
label: Blount's welcome at Knoxville

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of the letter or of this report, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of Senator William Blount's intercepted letter to the interpreter James Carey (July 1797): the letter as a document, and a Philadelphia report that introduces and quotes it. The wider Blount affair coverage is not included.
label: Blount letter made public

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the explanation of the British order in council of 26 April 1809 given by the Board of Trade to a committee of merchants trading to America: 'By this regulation the United States may trade without interruption from British cruisers, with all the ports of Russia, Norway, and Sweden', the Baltic and other coasts. The papers printed it in different settings: as the Board's explanation ('Their Lordships state'), at the end of a London report of 28 April on the merchants' meeting with the lords of trade, or in a paragraph beginning 'It appears by the modification of the orders in council'. The British government's explanation, as reported from London.
label: The Board of Trade's explanation of the order of 26 April

admission_rule: Reviewed 1800 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the first part of the correspondence on Bonaparte's offer of peace, as the British government published it: Talleyrand's letter to Lord Grenville sending a messenger ('I dispatch by order of General Buonaparte, first Consul of the French Republic, a messenger to London'), the First Consul's letter to the King ('Called by the wishes of the French nation to occupy the first magistracy of the Republic, I think it proper, on entering into office, to make a direct communication of it to your Majesty'), and Lord Grenville's note of 4 January 1800 in answer ('The King has given frequent proofs of his sincere desire for the re-establishment of secure and permanent tranquillity in Europe'), which declines to negotiate. The same papers printed the second part, Talleyrand's reply of 14 January and Lord Grenville's of 20 January, a week or two later (not admitted; see the README). Each government's own letters.
label: Bonaparte's letter to the King of Great Britain, 25 December 1799, and Lord Grenville's answer

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from headquarters at Cambridge, 19 March 1776, reporting that the British army left Boston on 17 March.
label: Boston evacuated

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of General Bournonville's letter to the French Executive Directory from Mulheim, dated 3 Brumaire (two papers add 'Oct. 28'): 'I had the honor to give you an account yesterday of the attack of the army made by the enemy in the night between the 29th and 30th Vendemiaire ... upon the head of the bridge and the isle of Neuwied'; he writes that the enemy meant to make the garrison prisoners of war, and that 'This affair cost the enemy more than four thousand men'. Printed from the Paris papers, in the same column as Truguet's letter of 6 November (a group of its own). A commander's own report.
label: General Bournonville to the Directory, Mulheim, 3 Brumaire: the attack on the bridgehead at Neuwied

admission_rule: Existing inspected selections only; additional candidates require an explicit documented admission.
definition: Reports, printed challenge and later related account concerning the expedition; not a single verified event.
label: Boyd / Bantry coverage

admission_rule: Existing inspected selections only; additional candidates require an explicit documented admission.
definition: Corresponding core fleet report; includes the edition with an appended challenge.
label: Boyd fleet report

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a paragraph from London papers of February 1806: 'A private letter from Bremen of the 11th inst. contains the following article, relative to the sentences passed on the officers whose conduct produced the recent misfortunes to the House of Austria'. A report at second hand, from a private letter.
label: A Bremen letter on the sentences of the Austrian officers

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).
definition: Printings of a New York report of late July 1793 on the brig Mary, Captain Langdon, from Cap Français, which she left on 9 July: her forty passengers said that from six to nine hundred people lost their lives 'in the affair of the 20th' (most papers add 'instead of 10 thousand as we heard'; the Patowmac Guardian prints 'two thousand'), that not more than two thirds of the town was burnt, that 'upwards of 20,000 mulattoes and blacks are now under arms there', that 'the negroes never came in from the country on the late occasion', and that the Spaniards had taken a town and were on the march. The passengers' account, at second hand.
label: The brig Mary's passengers on Cap Français

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a London paragraph of October 1807: the British ministers had delivered to Monroe and Pinkney their final answer on the leading points in dispute, so that 'the question of peace or war with America' was decided as far as it could be in England, and Monroe was preparing to leave. It is a London paper's report and forecast.
label: London: 'the question of peace or war'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a New York report of May 1809, by the ship Projector from Canton: 'an expedition fitted out at Bengal and Penang, under the direction of admiral Drury, for the purpose of taking possession of Macao', had arrived in September 1808, and the Portuguese governor refused to surrender the place. A report at second hand.
label: News from Canton: Admiral Drury's expedition to Macao

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The House of Representatives and the President on stopping imports from Great Britain in 1806, as the papers printed it: Mr. Gregg's resolution, Mr. J. Randolph's speech against it, the National Intelligencer's paragraph on the vote for Mr. Nicholson's resolution, the act of 18 April prohibiting certain British goods, and the President's message of 3 December asking that the act be suspended. Contains those five groups.
label: Congress and British goods, 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the King's instructions to the commanders of British ships of war and privateers (Windsor, 11 April 1808): they were not to interrupt neutral vessels laden with lumber and provisions bound to the British colonies, under the conditions the instructions set.
label: British instructions of 11 April on provisions for the colonies

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the British order in council of 26 April 1809, from the London Gazette of 29 April: 'At the Court at the Queen's Palace, the 26th of April, 1809 ... Whereas his Majesty, by his order in council of the 11th November, 1807, was pleased ... to order' the restrictions of a blockade; the order revokes those orders and in their place puts the ports of France, Holland and Italy, and their colonies, under blockade. The British government's order.
label: The British order in council of 26 April 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two items on British orders concerning American vessels that carried the produce of the enemy's colonies, as the papers printed them from September 1805: a London paragraph of 7 and 8 August reporting an order to detain such vessels, and the Privy Council's minute of 3 August as the British consuls published it in November. Contains those two groups.
label: British orders on American vessels carrying colonial produce, 1805

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Documents the President sent to Congress in January 1806 on the capture of American vessels and the impressment of American seamen by Britain: his message of 17 January, the letter of the American minister in London to Lord Mulgrave that was sent with it, and the Secretary of State's report on 'new principles interpolated into the law of nations'. Contains those three groups.
label: British seizures and impressment: papers sent to Congress, January 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of this report, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of Captain Kennard's report that the brig Brothers was boarded by a privateer on the way from Grenada to Portsmouth, N.H. (September 1797). Not independently verified.
label: Brothers boarded by privateer

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 reports of the fire or of Brown's death, checked against the scan.
definition: Reports of the fire at the Philadelphia house of the printer Andrew Brown (27 January 1797) and notices of his death a week later. Several different texts.
label: Andrew Brown house fire

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a London paragraph of September 1806: 'The official news of the capture of Buenos Ayres is received. It capitulated on the 27th of June. There fell into the hands of the English 1,291,338 dollars'. A report from the British side.
label: London, September 1806: Buenos Ayres captured

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two reports from Buenos Ayres printed by American papers in 1809, grouped by subject: a London paragraph of 12 June 'announcing the total defeat and submission of Liniers', and an extract of a letter from Rio de Janeiro of 3 August that a new Spanish viceroy had arrived and that Liniers 'gave up the government quietly'. Contains those two groups. Reports at second hand.
label: Buenos Ayres, 1809: reports of Liniers giving up the government

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the 66th bulletin of the French Grand Army (Osterode, 14 March 1807): the army rests in cantonments, with skirmishes between the outposts. New York papers had it by the brig Alonzo from Bordeaux, with the 65th.
label: The French army's 66th bulletin

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an abstract of the 78th bulletin of the French Grand Army (Heilsberg, 12 June 1807), received at Boston from Nantes: the overtures of peace made in the winter, broken off by the Russian attacks, and the action of Spanden on 5 June.
label: The 78th bulletin: the action of Spanden

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of a Burlington (Vermont) paragraph of 5 August 1808, headed 'Melancholy Event': a revenue cutter with a lieutenant, a sergeant and twelve privates, sent by the collector of the customs after a large boat 'well known to have been some time employed in smuggling', took her on Onion river; men on the bank then fired on the cutter's crew, and two of the crew and a man of the town were killed. The report says that eight persons were taken and put in gaol, that a jury of inquest found 'wilful murder', and that 'all opinion' should be suspended until the facts were known. A local report.
label: 'Melancholy Event': Burlington, Vermont, August 1808

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Documents and reports of Aaron Burr's alleged conspiracy and his trial, as the 1807 papers printed them: the President's message to Congress of 22 January, a New York report of news from New Orleans (February), Chief Justice Marshall's opinion on committing Burr (April), the jury's verdict in the treason trial (September), and Marshall's opinion of 20 October after the trial. Contains those five groups; the wider coverage is not included. The message and the reports carry allegations; the jury found the charge of treason not proved.
label: Burr's conspiracy and trial

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of President Jefferson's message to Congress of 22 January 1807, sent at the request of the House, on 'an illegal combination of private individuals' against the peace of the Union and a military expedition planned against Spanish territory, with the measures taken to suppress it. It names Aaron Burr as the principal actor. Its enclosures (General Wilkinson's affidavit and letters) are not counted separately.
label: The President's message on the conspiracy

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The first widely printed items on Aaron Burr's enterprise in the West, November 1806: a Chillicothe report of an affidavit against him in Kentucky, and the President's proclamation of 27 November against a military expedition against the dominions of Spain. Contains those two groups.
label: Colonel Burr's enterprise in the papers, November 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a New York report (3 February 1807) of news from New Orleans brought by the brig Neptune: General Wilkinson had refused Burr passage, the city was under arms, and Burr was said to be at Natchez with 600 men and an advanced guard of 200 cavalry. The numbers are a report, not an observed fact.
label: News from New Orleans: 'Burr in arms'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the jury's written verdict in Aaron Burr's trial for treason at Richmond on 1 September 1807, 'We of the jury find that Aaron Burr is not proved to be guilty under this indictment by any evidence submitted to us. We therefore find him not guilty', quoted in accounts of that day's proceedings, with Burr's objection to its form. Three different accounts carry it; most papers printed the same one.
label: The verdict: 'not proved to be guilty'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round two, 6-paper threshold for 1793).
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from a gentleman at Cadiz to his brother in New York, dated 24 June 1793 (New York, 12 August): 'a hot war with the Spaniards and French', a battle near Malaga reported won by the French, and news of the fleets. One writer's account, partly hearsay ('We had accounts').
label: A letter from Cadiz, 24 June: 'a hot war with the Spaniards and French'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a New York report of 25 March 1809 on the arrival of the ship Bordeaux, 51 days from Cadiz: her master's account, given 'verbally', that the English army had been 'attacked near Valladolid' and was retreating towards Corunna and that the American vessels at Algeciras were to be released, followed by an abstract furnished by the supercargo. Two papers printed a shorter New York paragraph ('We learn by a gentleman who arrived here yesterday from Cadiz'). Reports at second hand.
label: News from Cadiz by the ship Bordeaux: a battle near Valladolid

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the dispatch of Vice-Admiral Sir Robert Calder to Admiral Cornwallis, 'Prince of Wales, July 23, 1805', from the London Gazette: 'Yesterday at noon ... I was favored with a view of the combined squadrons of France and Spain, consisting of 20 sail of the line'; he 'brought on an action which lasted upwards of four hours' and took two ships. The British commander's own account.
label: Admiral Calder's dispatch on the action of 22 July

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of Lieutenant Colonel Campbell's letter to General Howe (Boston, 19 June 1776), reporting that he and two companies of Highlanders had been taken in Boston harbour.
label: Campbell's letter after his capture

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings of the dispatches, checked against the scan (opening only).
definition: Printings of Admiral Duncan's official dispatches on the defeat of the Dutch fleet off Camperdown (11 October 1797), from the London Gazette Extraordinary. Earlier first-news reports are not included.
label: Duncan's Camperdown dispatches

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a London newspaper report of 24 May 1809, headed 'AMERICAN AFFAIRS' and brought by way of Halifax: in the House of Commons 'lord Henry Petty put a question to Mr. Canning', who replied that the agreement made by Mr. Erskine 'was not made in conformity with the wishes of his majesty nor such as his majesty could approve of', and that American merchants who had acted on it would be protected. A newspaper's report of debate.
label: London, 24 May 1809: Canning tells the Commons the agreement was not authorised

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

label: Marshall's opinion on committing Burr

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.

label: Marshall's opinion of 20 October

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1800 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1800 printings, checked against the scan.

label: General Melas's letter summoning Massena to surrender Genoa, 1800

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of President Jefferson's annual message to Congress of 8 November 1808: the overtures to Britain and France had failed, their edicts stood, and Congress was to decide what course to take on the embargo.
label: The President's message of 8 November

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

label: The President's message to the Senate of 15 June 1809, with letters of Mr. Pinkney and Mr. Canning

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

A report at second hand.
label: 'Miranda defeated': Captain Foster's report from Trinidad

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings about the expedition that General Francisco de Miranda fitted out at New York in the ship Leander for the coast of Caracas, as the papers printed them through 1806: questions put to the Secretary of State in February, a letter from on board the Leander in April, Miranda's proclamation of 28 June, and a report of the expedition's defeat in November. Contains those four groups.
label: General Miranda's expedition, 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the proclamation that General Miranda issued on 28 June 1806 ('published at Trinidad', in one paper's words): 'FRIENDS AND COUNTRYMEN, The glorious opportunity now presents itself of relieving from oppression and arbitrary government, a people who are worthy of a better fate'. The expedition's own appeal.
label: General Miranda's proclamation of 28 June: 'Friends and Countrymen'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a paragraph headed 'MOREAU' in most papers, from a London paper: 'It has been announced in the Paris Moniteur, (the government paper) that this General has been banished to America—to what part is not suggested. label: 'It has been announced in the Paris Moniteur ... that this General has been banished to America': a London paragraph on Moreau, 1804

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the letter of James Monroe and William Pinkney from London, 27 December 1806, to the Secretary of State: they had agreed with the British commissioners to conclude a treaty on all the points of their negotiation, on terms they trusted the government would approve. label: Monroe and Pinkney: a treaty agreed

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the letter of James Monroe, the American minister in London, to Lord Mulgrave of the British government, dated Great Cumberland Place, 23 September 1805, sent to Congress with the President's message of 17 January 1806: 'I flattered myself, from what passed in our last interview, that I should have been honored' with an answer. The American minister's case against the British courts' decisions on neutral trade.
label: Monroe's letter to Lord Mulgrave, 23 September 1805

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of General Montgomery's letter to Governor Carleton from before Quebec, dated December 1775, calling on him to surrender the town.
label: Montgomery's letter to Carleton

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter dated 'Algiers, September 9, 1805', from Mr. Mountford, 'secretary of Mr. Lear, and now our charge d'affaires at Algiers', which General Eaton gave to the Enquirer: 'I have only a few moments to inform you, our affairs here are well. On the 30th ult. the soldiers rose in a body and murdered the Dey and his prime minister.' An American official's own short report; the words are his.
label: Mountford's letter from Algiers, 9 September

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the British answer, a letter from Lord Mulgrave to Talleyrand, the French minister of foreign affairs (January 1805): 'His Majesty has received the letter which has been addressed to him by the chief of the French government'; the King cannot answer it more particularly before communicating with the powers of the continent, in particular the Emperor of Russia. Britain's own letter.
label: Lord Mulgrave's answer to Talleyrand

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the letter of the Emperor Napoleon to the King of England, Paris, 12 Nivose year 13 (2 January 1805): 'Sir, my brother, Called to the throne of France by Providence, by the suffrages of the senate, the people and the army, my first sentiment is the wish of peace.' France's own letter: a proposal of peace and its argument.
label: Napoleon's letter to the King of England

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: The two letters that the French minister of foreign affairs laid before the French Senate on 4 February 1805, as the papers printed them from April: the Emperor Napoleon's letter to the King of England of 2 January 1805, proposing peace, and Lord Mulgrave's answer to Talleyrand. Contains those two groups; each is one government's own letter.
label: Napoleon's letter to the King of England and the British answer

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the Emperor Napoleon's proclamation to his army after the battle of 2 December 1805, dated Austerlitz, 12 Frimaire: 'Soldiers, I am satisfied with you'; an army of 100,000 men 'has been in less than four hours cut to pieces and dispersed'. A commander's address to his own army.
label: The Emperor's proclamation to the army after the battle

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the speech of the Emperor Napoleon at the opening of the French Legislative Body in March 1806: 'Since your last session, the greatest part of Europe has entered into a coalition with England. My armies have never ceased to conquer'. A head of state's own account.
label: The Emperor Napoleon's speech opening the Legislative Body, March 1806

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the speech of the Emperor Napoleon to the French Senate in September 1805, from Paris papers: 'Senators, In the present circumstances of Europe, I feel the necessity of appearing in the midst of you, and of making known to you my sentiments'; he is about to leave his capital to put himself at the head of the army. A head of state's own account. The Norfolk Gazette prints another translation ('I come among you to communicate my sentiments'), counted with the others.
label: Napoleon's speech to the French Senate, September 1805

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of the Nashville Clarion's account of 20 October 1809: 'To record the untimely end of a brave and prudent officer, a learned scholar and scientific gentleman this column of the Clarion is ushered to the world in black. On the night of the 10th instant Meriwether Lewis, esq. Governor-general of Upper Louisiana, on his way to Washington city', died at a house on the road; the paper says 'he had shot himself', and adds a sketch of his career. A newspaper's account.
label: The Nashville Clarion on the death of Governor Meriwether Lewis, October 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a letter from a gentleman at Nassau, New Providence, dated 26 September 1797, as a Columbia (South Carolina) paper printed it on 3 November: 'We have lately very providentially escaped a most hellish plot.—A parcel of French negroes who had been captured and sold here, and who had ran away from their owners, entered into a conspiracy (about thirty in number) to burn the town and make a general massacre of the whites.' By his account one of them told his master a few hours before, five were taken and condemned and three executed. One correspondent's account, written from the side of those who held the accused; the accused are heard only through it, and it names no one.
label: A letter from Nassau, New Providence, 26 September 1797: the writer's account of a 'plot'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter dated 7 August 1804, published at Natchez on 10 August: 'Returning this morning from the vicinity of Little Bayou-Sara, I met not far from the line, 21 armed men;—on passing a house within my view, they sounded a French horn, and unfurled a flag composed of four white and three blue stripes'. Two papers print it under the heading 'Unpleasant Symptoms'. An unsigned letter-writer's own account.
label: Natchez, August 1804: a letter of 7 August on armed men with a flag near Bayou Sara

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

A report at second hand from a traveller, with the party's own declaration.
label: Natchez, 14 August 1804: 'Mr. Nathan Kemper, with a party of about 30 men, with colors flying and horns sounding' marches on Baton Rouge

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

label: The National Intelligencer's paragraph of 19 April 1809 on the arrangement

admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of a Washington paragraph of 29 July 1807 from the National Intelligencer: 'Much error having appeared in the accounts circulated' of what passed between the government and the British minister, Erskine, 'in the case of the seamen, to obtain whom the Leopard made the late attack on the Chesapeake', it states that his application for their surrender was refused, that naval commanders had orders not to recruit British deserters, and that the government had reason to believe the seamen were native citizens of the United States. The National Intelligencer's own account; it adds a note with the seamen's names and particulars as Captain Barron reported them.
label: The National Intelligencer on the seamen the Leopard sought

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

label: The National Intelligencer on the vote of 17 March

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

In four papers it is a letter that opens by accusing two named men of 'exciting sedition among the troops'. One side's account; it names soldiers as accused.
label: An account from New Orleans of a planned revolt at the camp of Terre-aux-Boeufs, July 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

label: A report from Martinique that the Toulon fleet was captured, July 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1793 printings, checked against the scan (round three: stories once held back for framing, at the 6-paper threshold for 1793).

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

label: A Norfolk report of 25 February 1804: 'DEPLORABLE AND DISTRESSING FIRE!!'

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.

label: The British order in council of 4 July: peace with Spain

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan.

definition: Printings of a communication first printed in the Philadelphia Gazette of 19 February 1806: 'SERIOUS QUESTIONS TO MR. MADISON. It asks what the government knew of the ship Leander, fitted out at New York for General Miranda's expedition. Questions that carry an allegation, by an unnamed writer.
label: "Serious Questions to Mr. Madison" on General Miranda's expedition

admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).
definition: Printings of an extract of a letter of Governor Sevier of Tennessee to a friend at Staunton, Virginia, dated Marble Springs, 14 May 1808, first printed in the Staunton Eagle: an express from General Jackson had reported that '440 Creeks and 12 whites' had taken a position on the south bank of the Tennessee near the mouth of Duck river and had killed about twenty persons; 'If this be true we shall have warm work this summer'. The Eagle adds that two companies of West Tennessee militia were on duty on the frontier. A report at second hand, which the governor passes on with a condition.
label: Governor Sevier's letter from Marble Springs, May 1808

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Salem report of September 1805, headed in most papers 'Bloody Scenes at Algiers': 'Capt. Shillaber, from Leghorn, informs us, that on the 7th July a brig arrived there from Algiers, and brought accounts of an insurrection at that place'; a Leghorn letter of 8 July follows. News at third hand: a shipmaster repeats what a brig brought to Leghorn.
label: Salem report: Captain Shillaber's news of an insurrection at Algiers

admission_rule: Reviewed 1800 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two documents on the Austrian siege of Genoa, held by the French general Massena from April to June 1800, as the American papers printed them in July and August: the Austrian commander Melas's letter summoning Massena to surrender, and Massena's report to the First Consul of 7 June on the evacuation of the city under a convention. Contains those two groups.
label: The siege and evacuation of Genoa, 1800: Melas's summons and Massena's report

admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Williamsburg report (13 April 1776) that on 30 March the sloop Liberty of Perth Amboy, from St. Eustatius with 83 barrels of gunpowder, dry goods and medicines, was taken by a British tender off the capes and carried into Norfolk, with what her mate, who escaped, said of British troops at Antigua.
label: The sloop Liberty's gunpowder taken

admission_rule: Reviewed 1797 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Reports (September–October 1797) that the commissioner Sonthonax had sailed for France and Toussaint Louverture held the chief command.
label: Sonthonax leaves Saint-Domingue

admission_rule: Reviewed 1809 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two New York reports of October 1809 on Don Luis de Onis, sent to the United States as minister by the Spanish Junta: the arrival of the Spanish frigate Cornelia that brought him, and the paragraph of 25 October that 'The new Spanish Minister, Don Onis, has not been received by our government.' Contains those two groups. Reports.
label: The Spanish envoy Onis arrives and is not received, October 1809

admission_rule: Reviewed 1804 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Two publications in a dispute between the Marquis de Casa Yrujo, the Spanish minister to the United States, and W. Jackson of the Philadelphia Political Register, in September and October 1804: Jackson's statement with a deposition and letters, and the minister's letter to the Secretary of State in reply. Each side's own account. Contains those two groups.
label: The Spanish minister Yrujo and W. Jackson of the Political Register, September and October 1804

admission_rule: Reviewed 1800 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a Spanish royal order, published at Cadiz on 28 February 1800 and sent by the American consul there, headed 'Blockade of Gibraltar' in most papers (the Republican Ledger heads it 'Blockade of Cadiz'): 'His Catholic Majesty desirous of lessening as far as possible the injuries resulting to the Nation by the shameful trade carried on by many of his subjects with Gibraltar' orders that vessels bound to or from Gibraltar be treated as enemies. The Spanish government's order, as the consul sent it.
label: The King of Spain's order of February 1800 against trade with Gibraltar

admission_rule: Reviewed 1805 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Printings of a royal order dated 'Madrid, Sept. 3, 1805' (5 September in some papers), as the Spanish commander of marine at Algeziras received it and a Gibraltar paper printed it: 'His Excellency, the Minister of the United States, has complained of new grievances and captures of American vessels by the Spanish privateers; and that eleven Americans have been carried into Algeziras'; vessels taken only for carrying English goods are to be released. The Spanish government's own order, at second hand.
label: A royal order from Madrid on American vessels carried into Algeziras

admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.
definition: Letters printed from September to November 1806 on Spanish troops east of the Sabine and the American army sent against them: a letter of 2 August headed 'HOSTILE APPEARANCE', a Natchitoches letter on Mr. Freeman's exploring party, and a letter of General Wilkinson.
